newsitem.title: USA: Calif. local govts join suit against tobacco cos.
newsitem.headline: Calif. local govts join suit against tobacco cos.

text.p: Eleven local governments in California joined San Francisco to sue major tobacco companies to try to recover the costs of treating smoking-related illnesses, attorneys said on Friday.
In June, the city and county of San Francisco became the first local government entities in the U.S. to sue the tobacco industry when it filed its complaint in U.S. District Court.

At the time, San Francisco said other local governments in the state were considering joining the case. Friday, San Francisco deputy city attorney Elizabeth Laporte said the federal suit was amended to include 10 other counties.
They are Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Sacramento, San Bernardino, San Mateo, Santa Barbara, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz and Shasta.
The amended suit, filed Thursday in U.S. District Court, seeks unspecified damages.

"We welcome all the counties and cities joining because it shows just how important and serious this public health issue is. Even if our (state) Attorney General won't act, local governments will," said Laporte, chief of special litigation.
She said a second lawsuit was filed Thursday by San Francisco in Superior Court. It includes San Francisco, the 10 counties in the other complaint, and city of San Jose.

The state court suit, filed under state consumer protection statutes, seeks to stop such marketing practices by tobacco companies as the alleged targeting of minors, and seeks disgorgement of profits, and penalties.
The state court complaint could include disgorgement of profits from tobacco sales statewide, Laporte said.
Laporte said it was possible that other counties and cities in the state would join in the lawsuits.
In June, Los Angeles County's Board of Supervisors also voted to sue the tobacco industry. That suit has not been joined with San Francisco's lawsuits.
Between San Francisco, its co-plaintiffs and Los Angeles, Laporte said over half the state population was represented.
Fourteen states have sued the industry to recoup health care costs of smokers.

The San Francisco lawsuits target Brown & Williamson Corp, American Tobacco Co and parent B.A.T Industries Plc, Philip Morris Cos Inc, and R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
Other defendants are Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group Inc, Loews Corp's Lorillard Tobacco Co, Council for Tobacco Research and Tobacco Institute.
San Francisco's federal court suit alleged the tobacco companies suppressed and concealed information about the health consequences of cigarette smoking.

Laporte said the counties represented in the suit spend millions of dollars each year on health care for people who have tobacco-related illnesses and on insurance for the treatment of workers with such illnesses.
If the lawsuits are successful, the companies could be forced to pay hundreds of millions of dollars, Laporte said.
The suits seek orders requiring the companies to stop the alleged targeting of youths in their advertising and to make public their research on smoking addiction and health.
